feature: Fixed identity headroom in the classic entry budget
scope: The nightly release stamps the candidate version and source identity into the classic entry before the size gate measures it. The 2026-11-26 scheduled run measured 1222727 bytes against the 1222725-byte cap, so the entry was sitting exactly on its measured local size. ENTRY_IDENTITY_HEADROOM adds 512 raw bytes to BUDGET.bytes and nothing else: the gzip cap, the legacy, base and complete payload caps, every provider and optional asset cap and the module inventory stay unchanged.

incident.error: Classic bundle validation failed: 1 size violations; dist/player.js: asset bytes 1222727 exceeds budget 1222725

growthAttribution.method: Paired npm run build plus node scripts/measure-classic-composition.cjs at 80f56b37 (the parent of the slot-addressed Edem provider settings feature) and at the pre-headroom head ed7736c0. Module figures are the production optimizer attribution of the emitted entry, so they sum to the artifact delta.
growthAttribution.conclusion: The slot-addressed Edem provider settings feature accounts for the entire recent entry growth. Its 47f59a53 allowance of 484 raw bytes replaced the previous cap with a measured-size cap instead of preserving the 2026-11-25 headroom, so 110 bytes separated the local build from the cap and the identity-stamped nightly artifact crossed it by 2.

limits: Same source, unstamped local build versus the stamped local release-envelope replica.
Same feature, unstamped local build versus the separately identified nightly artifact; a net pair across builds, not a controlled isolation.

identityCost.note: Identity stamping alone was worth between 76 and 151 bytes on the same source, more than the 73 bytes left under the old cap and more than the 2-byte overrun suggested.

reason: 512 raw bytes is about three times the largest observed identity cost (151 bytes) and stays a named, round figure instead of a fit to one failing build. The gzip cap already carried roughly 1.5 KiB of headroom, so it does not move. Only the entry is charged: legacy, base and complete payloads keep their own reserves and the headroom is counted once in BUDGET.
validation: node scripts/check-release-envelope-size.cjs rebuilt the entry with the release version suffix and revision stamp: 1222652 bytes against the 1223237-byte cap before the helper change, PASS.

tests/test_classic_size.cjs and tests/test_classic_size_diagnostics.cjs exclude ENTRY_IDENTITY_HEADROOM from the historical projections, as already done for later allowances, so docs/evidence receipts stay comparable.
tests/test_release_envelope_size.cjs still passes; the headroom is not counted in the provider, optional or per-family caps.
limitations: The nightly measurement comes from a different build identity than the local builds, so the 151-byte identity figure is an observed net pair and bounds the stamp cost rather than isolating it.
The margin is a budget change, not a size reduction: a later feature that consumes it still needs its own measured allowance.
